title: Did anyone actually arb tokenized GOOGL vs real GOOGL post-earnings?
author: Odd_Classic_5351
selftext:
Google missed. The tokenized stock dumped first, then the real stock opened lower. Arb kept the two roughly in line, but there must have been a window. Did anyone here actually trade that gap?

I’m not looking for theory. I’m looking for real fills: which venue, how fast, what fees/funding/borrow/slippage killed the edge, and whether it was actually worth it. If you’ve done this in practice, please share. Thanks.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: no fills to share, but the leg that usually eats it is the real-stock side: overnight GOOGL trades on thin venues and most brokers won't let you short it before the open. which venue had the tokenized side?

comments.author: CapoDoFrango
comments.body: did you checked the price after hours or pre market? your phrase of "opened lower" seems a bit naive. It opened just where the pre-market price was at that moment: [https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/06/preaftermarket.asp](https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/06/preaftermarket.asp)
